_help.about: (Claude Code, 6 Oct, LOCKED by Mike: the dungeon's fitted-stone walls; FittedStone, TombBuild) Every tomb wall's seen face is cut into irregular polygonal stones (a Voronoi partition of the wall's plane: Incan ashlar, Sacsayhuamán), each a real piece of geometry, no normal maps (LOOK_REFERENCE): its face pushed proud of the wall and pillowed (gently convex), its edges bevelled down into thin recessed joints that sit in shadow. Tight fit: neighbours share edges, no mortar. A minority are settled (a little out or in, a slight turn, an occasional sink) so the wall reads old. The overgrowth follows the place's damp: moss in the joints and on the shaded lower wall, vines from cracks and wall tops where it's wet; bare stone and drifted dust in the corners where it's dry. Restart after editing.
_help.preset: Which of presets every wall uses: megalithic (few big blocks, Sacsayhuamán) or fitted_small (many tight stones; design §EU.5 spells it so, and "fitted-small" is read as the same).
_help.seed: 0: from the tomb's own seed (each tomb its own stones); any other number pins the stone layout.
_help.presets: Per preset: cell_m the average stone's height (m); aspect its width over its height (Incan courses run wide); jitter 0-1 how far each stone's seed point strays from a regular grid (1: wild polygons, 0: a brick bond); joint_m the joint's width between neighbours; joint_depth_m how far the joint's back sits behind the wall's face (its shadow); bevel_m the width of each stone's rounded edge running down into the joint; proud_m how far a stone's face stands out from the wall's face; pillow_m how much more its middle bulges (the convex face); settle_share the share of stones settled (the rest flush), settle_out_m how far one sits out or in, settle_rot_deg how far it turns in the wall's plane, sink_share and sink_m an occasional stone sunk a little lower; tint a colour multiplied over the stone (white keeps the ruins' palette).
_help.humidity: How damp each part of the tomb is (0 dry - 1 wet), which drives the overgrowth: by_theme the base for a theme (crawler.json themes), vary how much it wanders from place to place (smooth noise over scale_m), per_flight how much wetter each flight of stairs down makes it. So areas differ on their own.
_help.overgrowth: density scales it all (0 none). Damp: moss from wet_from, full at wet_full: in the joints (joint_moss) and on the lower wall up to low_wall_m (low_moss, fading upward), and vines (vines_per_m along a wall, vine_len_m long) hanging from the wall's top and from cracks. Dry, under dry_below: no moss or vines; drifted dust or sand in corners and along the foot (dust_per_m drifts a metre of wall, dust_h_m high), dust_color.
